name: @oyah/mcp

tools.name: read_board
tools.description: Read the live Oyah board as JSON. With no narrowing it returns an INDEX: every outcome (ref, title, status, measure) and its Steps as ref, title, kind and status — no Step fields — plus boards, card types and the sprint in outline. Narrow it to read what you need in full: `refs` for named cards with all their fields, their outcome and their linked cards one hop away (blocks, blockedBy, relates); `outcome` for one outcome with its Steps listed; `sprint` for the running and planned sprints' cards. Without `set` it reads the board set open on screen; name a set to read another. Read before writing any op: cards are referenced by their ref.

set.description: A board set by name. Omit for the open set.

refs.description: Cards to read in full, e.g. ["ABC-123"].

outcome.description: One outcome by ref: its fields and its Steps listed.

sprint.description: true: the running and planned sprints, their cards listed.

tools.name: card_moves
tools.description: For each card, its type, its status and every move out of that status under the card type's OWN process (the board's settings, not a fixed list): whether the move is ready, the field rules an op will REFUSE it on until met, the other rules the board's gate waits on, and advice. Call it before a setStatus so you meet the rules first instead of learning them from a refusal.

tools.name: apply_ops
tools.description: Apply a batch of board ops and get the result back in this reply: every op's outcome in order, with the error text of any that failed and the ref of every card it created or changed. Ops include addOutcome, addStep, setField, appendField, setStatus, setSubset, addCardDep, addToSprint and renameCard. Deletions and re-plans (deleteStep, deleteOutcome, moveStep) belong in delete_or_replan; sent here they are HELD, the whole batch with them, until a person approves it in Oyah, and read_board shows what became of it under "held". Within one batch, a card created earlier is reached by its title, never its ref (refs are minted after the batch). When you have built a card, tick each criterion you verified: { "op": "tickAcceptance", "ref": "ABC-12", "n": 2, "by": "assistant", "evidence": "the check that passed, or a one-line result" } (refused without evidence). The tester sees it as checked by you and only tries what is left. Never tick what only a person can judge (it looks right, it reads well, it goes where they expect). A NEW PROJECT, planned, is one op: { "op": "planProject", "name": "Setlist", "idea": "the person's own words", "objective": "what the first version achieves, and for whom", "milestones": [{ "title": "what this milestone achieves", "by": "YYYY-MM-DD", "why": "…", "keyResults": [{ "name": "Bands sharing a setlist", "measuredIn": "bands", "now": "0", "target": "5" }], "aims": [{ "title": "what people will be able to do", "outcomes": [{ "title": "…", "measure": "…", "baseline": "0", "target": "…", "why": "…" }] }] }] }. Two or three milestones; the first with its Aims and two to four outcomes, later ones may have no Aims yet. It refuses a name already taken. Accept what the person accepts in chat with { "op": "acceptPlan", "forProject": "Setlist" } or acceptProposal (forProject plus one of objective: true, milestone, aim, outcome or ref); discard what they reject with discardProposal (same targeting), which takes what is still proposed under the piece with it and is refused over anything accepted.

tools.name: delete_or_replan
tools.description: Delete cards (deleteStep, deleteOutcome) or re-plan a card onto another outcome (moveStep), and get the result back in this reply. Your tool asks the person before this call runs: that answer is the approval, and the ops apply at once. Only these three ops, in a batch of their own. Same op shapes as in apply_ops, e.g. { "op": "deleteStep", "ref": "ABC-12" } or { "op": "moveStep", "ref": "ABC-12", "toOutcomeRef": "ABC-3" }.

tools.name: show
tools.description: Bring a card (by ref) or a board (by name, e.g. "Backlog") into view in every open copy of Oyah, without changing anything — use it when you start talking about a card or the queue. A copy with Follow on moves to it; one with Follow off shows a "Claude is on … · Show" note instead. apply_ops already brings the card it changed into view, so there is no need to show that one.

board.description: A board by the name on screen, e.g. "Backlog". The open set's board of that name is shown.

instructions:
Oyah is the team's board; these tools reach the open Oyah app.
- Read before you write: read_board first, and address cards by their ref (the code on each card, e.g. ABC-123).
- Before moving a card's status, call card_moves for it. It lists what that card type's own process asks before each move:
  "op refuses" rules must be met first (write the field earlier in the same batch, before the setStatus);
  "board asks" and "advice" are the team's rules too — meet them, or say plainly that you moved without them.
- Each apply_ops reply is the record of what landed. Report from it, never from memory, and fix any FAIL before saying the work is recorded.
- A rename (renameCard) is an ordinary op: send it with apply_ops.
- Deletions and re-plans (deleteStep, deleteOutcome, moveStep) go through delete_or_replan, on their own. Your tool asks the
  person before that call runs, so their yes IS the approval and the ops apply at once. Use it only for what the person
  asked for, or say plainly that you are proposing it.
- Sent through apply_ops instead, those ops are HELD in Oyah for a person to approve, with the whole batch. read_board
  lists held batches under "held" with their state (waiting, approved, declined).

Plan a new app first. Oyah exists to help the person plan before you build:
- When they ask you to build something new and no Oyah project covers it (read_board lists the workspace's "projects"),
  offer to plan it in Oyah first, in a line or two, before writing any code. If they say no, carry on as you would
  without Oyah and create nothing.
- Ask questions only when the idea is too thin to plan from, and then only two or three plain ones (who is it for, what
  would make a first version a win). If it does not say where it runs, ask whether it is for the web, phones or both:
  that changes the milestones. Otherwise propose straight away.
- Propose the WHOLE plan with one apply_ops op, planProject (its shape is in apply_ops). Every outcome carries a measure:
  a number that moves when the outcome works. Everything it makes is PROPOSED until the person accepts it.
- Then say in a few plain sentences what you proposed, and that it is on the project's Aim board in Oyah to accept, change
  or discard. Talk in their words, not Oyah's: they learn Objective, Milestone and Key Result by seeing them on the board.
- Build only once the plan is accepted (read_board shows "proposed" on what is not). If they accept or reject it in chat,
  send acceptPlan, acceptProposal or discardProposal; never accept or discard on their behalf otherwise.
- Once the plan is accepted, before building the first outcome, offer to talk about the look and the tech first (apps they
  like, the feel; where it runs, what they already use), and say you will pick sensible defaults if they skip. Either way,
  write the answers, or the defaults you chose, to the product with updateProduct { product, designBrief, stack: "custom",
  customStack, contextNotes }, so they are kept in Oyah and can be changed there. read_board shows them under "products";
  read them before you write any Step's Design.
